title: IRGC claims it destroyed Amazon's Bahrain data center
titleZh: IRGC 声称摧毁了亚马逊巴林数据中心
author: thisislife2
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: IRGC claims cruise missile strike destroyed AWS Bahrain data center in Wave 24, citing Darkhovin nuclear plant as casus belli. Third strike on same facility since March. July 21, 2026 MANAMA — The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed on July 21 that it struck and destroyed Amazon Web Services’ data center in Bahrain with cruise missiles, in stated retaliation for the US strike on Iran’s Darkhovin nuclear power plant two days earlier. The claim, carried by IRNA, Tasnim, and Iran International but unconfirmed by Amazon or CENTCOM, would mark the first use of cruise missiles against commercial cloud infrastructure in the Gulf conflict and at least the third kinetic action against the same AWS facility since March. Day 149 since Feb 28 Casualties 13,260+ 5 nations Brent Crude ● LIVE $113 ▲ 57% from $72 Hormuz Strait RESTRICTED 94% traffic drop Ships Hit 16 since Day 1

The IRGC packaged the data center strike alongside claimed hits on US air-defense radar at Muharraq and a Patriot battery at Riffa, treating Amazon’s commercial cloud as operationally equivalent to the military systems defending Bahrain’s airspace. For Saudi Arabia, which launched its own in-kingdom AWS region in Riyadh six months before the war began and still carries legacy workloads in Bahrain, the targeting logic the IRGC applied to a building twenty-five kilometres across the causeway now covers every piece of US-branded digital infrastructure in the Gulf — from Aramco’s cloud-integrated operational technology to NEOM’s planned 1.5-gigawatt data center campus.

Manama’s commercial district, where the Bahrain Financial Harbour and high-rise towers mark the Gulf’s most compact concentration of regional corporate headquarters. AWS ME-South-1, operational since July 2019, sits within the metropolitan area and was the primary cloud hub for Gulf enterprise and government customers until the war began. comments.author: dhx
comments.textRawHtml:
AWS's 3 data centres in me-south-1 are:

BAH53 (Manama): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492345589

  An adjoining substation to BAH53 had one of it's two main buildings damaged/destroyed about 2026-07-16 per https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-data-center-power-substation-bahrain-jul-16th-2026-142024

  Then about 2026-07-22 BAH53 itself was damaged/destroyed per https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-amazon-web-services-bahrain-jul-22nd-2026-142112

  Possibly the least defended of the three sites as there is no air/missile defence battery in between this site and Iran.
BAH54 (Zallaq): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1359931661

  No media reports about this data centre being attacked previously. Possibly the safest of the three as there are at least two (probably three) air/missile defence batteries in between this site and Iran.
BAH55 (Hamala): https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/956069872

  Apparently the Batelco DC.1 data centre adjoining (and apparently critical to) BAH55 was damaged/destroyed about 2026-04-01 per https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgk28nj0lrjo _or_ the adjoining substation to these two facilities was damaged/destroyed -- news articles are hard to follow as to what exactly might have been damaged and the extent of damage caused.

  Middle ground for defence with one or two (maybe three) air/missile defence batteries between this site and Iran, depending on where drones/missiles are launched from.
If these data centres are rebuilt, you'd maybe expect them to be rebuilt in new locations behind existing _permanent_ (and seemingly quite expensive) air/missile defence batteries in Bahrain (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492281507 and https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492953902). Based on the permanency of those air/missile defence batteries it doesn't look like the government of Bahrain are expecting things to get safer for data centre hosting in Bahrain any time soon.
comments.textZhHtml:
AWS 位于 me-south-1 的 3 个数据中心是：

BAH53（麦纳麦）：https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492345589

 BAH53 的相邻变电站的两座主要建筑之一受损/毁坏约2026 年 7 月 16 日，每 https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-data-center-power-substation-bahrain-jul-16th-2026-142024

  然后大约 2026 年 7 月 22 日，BAH53 本身根据 https://soaratlas.com/maps/asia-damage-to-amazon-web-services-bahrain-jul-22nd-2026-142112 被损坏/摧毁

  可能是三个地点中防御最薄弱的一个，因为该地点与伊朗之间没有防空/导弹防御系统。
BAH54 (Zallaq)：https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1359931661

 此前没有关于此数据中心遭受攻击的媒体报道。可能是三个中最安全的，因为该地点和伊朗之间至少有两个（可能是三个）防空/导弹防御连。
BAH55（哈马拉）：https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/956069872

 显然，BAH55 毗邻（并且显然对 BAH55 至关重要）的 Batelco DC.1 数据中心于 2026 年 4 月 1 日左右被损坏/毁坏，根据 https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgk28nj0lrjo _or_ 这两个设施的毗邻变电站损坏/毁坏——很难通过新闻文章了解到底什么可能被损坏以及造成的损坏程度。

  根据无人机/导弹的发射地点，在该地点和伊朗之间使用一到两个（也许三个）防空/导弹防御连进行防御的中间地带。
如果重建这些数据中心，您可能希望将它们重建在巴林现有_永久_（并且看起来相当昂贵）防空/导弹防御电池后面的新位置（https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492281507 和 https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1492953902）。根据这些防空/导弹防御电池的永久性，巴林政府似乎并不期望巴林的数据中心托管很快就会变得更安全。

children.author: dhx
children.textRawHtml: Update: IRGC published satellite imagery a few hours ago showing an impact to BAH54, apparently impacted on 2026-07-24, alongside another undated image before the impact. From a quick comparison of both images with reliable satellite imagery sources (e.g. WV02 image dated 2025-02-21 on ESRI World Imagery Wayback) there are no obvious signs of image manipulation, with roof features and surrounding buildings/other features lining up as expected. Additionally the claimed post-strike image adds a significant number of vehicles to the site (when there are usually close to none present), which may correspond to fire fighting vehicles expected to be monitoring the site afterwards. Further, Sentinel-2 imagery from 2026-07-24 shows a dark patch (blast damage) on the roof of BAH54 per https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?zoom=18&lat=26.0509...
children.textZhHtml: 更新：IRGC 几个小时前发布的卫星图像显示了对 BAH54 的影响，显然是在 2026 年 7 月 24 日受到影响，同时还有另一张未注明日期的影响前的图像。通过将两幅图像与可靠的卫星图像源（例如 ESRI World Imagery Wayback 上日期为 2025 年 2 月 21 日的 WV02 图像）进行快速比较，没有明显的图像处理迹象，屋顶特征和周围建筑物/其他特征按预期排列。此外，声称的袭击后图像在现场添加了大量车辆（而通常几乎没有车辆），这可能对应于预计事后监视现场的消防车。此外，2026 年 7 月 24 日的 Sentinel-2 图像显示 BAH54 屋顶上有一个黑色斑块（爆炸损坏），按照https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?zoom=18&lat=26.0509...

children.author: dhx
children.textRawHtml:
Update 2:

Upon checking Sentinel-2 imagery for BAH55 from 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-13 (and all later imagery) there is also visible blast damage to the roof of BAH55, which would correspond in timing to media reports about damage caused about 2026-04-01. Sentinel-2 imagery appears to clarify AWS' claim of "while in Bahrain, a drone strike in close proximity to one of our facilities" to mean a direct impact to the building. However it seems likely from high resolution satellite imagery of BAH55 that the machinery rooms of the building perhaps took most of the damage, perhaps leaving data halls in a better shape elsewhere in the building (but possibly still unusable due to water/smoke damage).

[1] https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?zoom=17&lat=26.156&...

[2] https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/?zoom=17&lat=26.156&...
children.textZhHtml:
更新 2：

在检查 2026 年 3 月 29 日至 2026 年 4 月 13 日期间 BAH55 的 Sentinel-2 图像（以及所有后续图像）时，BAH55 的屋顶也出现了明显的爆炸损坏，这与媒体报道的 2026 年 4 月 1 日左右造成的损坏的时间相对应。 Sentinel-2 图像似乎澄清了 AWS 的说法，即“在巴林期间，无人机袭击了我们的一处设施附近”，这意味着对建筑物的直接影响。然而，从 BAH55 的高分辨率卫星图像来看，建筑物的机房可能遭受了大部分损坏，也许建筑物其他地方的数据大厅状况较好（但可能由于水/烟损坏而仍然无法使用）。

children.author: palmotea
children.textRawHtml:
> If these data centres are rebuilt, you'd maybe expect them to be rebuilt in new locations behind existing _permanent_ (and seemingly quite expensive) air/missile defence batteries in Bahrain

I've seen data centers that were built to withstand an aircraft impact (they were located on a major airport flight path). I wonder if they'd rebuild these to that standard or something even stronger, given these attacks. It probably wouldn't help much against ballistic missiles, but it might make it more resilient against drone attacks.

Here's a Google Maps link to BAH53 (Manama), it doesn't look like the hardened data centers I seen (e.g. sloped walls like a bunker): https://maps.app.goo.gl/6DjhQs753p6EHQUu6
children.textZhHtml:
> 如果重建这些数据中心，您可能会期望将它们重建在巴林现有_永久_（并且看起来相当昂贵）防空/导弹防御电池后面的新位置

我见过一些数据中心是为了承受飞机撞击而建造的（它们位于主要机场的飞行路线上）。我想知道考虑到这些攻击，他们是否会按照该标准或更强大的标准重建它们。它可能对弹道导弹没有太大帮助，但可能会使其更能抵御无人机攻击。

这是 BAH53（麦纳麦）的 Google 地图链接，它不像看起来像我看到的加固数据中心（例如，像掩体一样的倾斜墙壁）：https://maps.app.goo.gl/6DjhQs753p6EHQUu6

children.author: yardstick
children.textRawHtml:
London has lots of datacentres in Slough (near Heathrow) and Docklands (London City Airport, but also many LHR planes transit over).

AWS/Azure/GCP/etc Colo in Equinix/Telehouse datacentres there, and those Docklands locations in particular were picked based on location to LINX (major London peering/interchange), and LINX was put in Docklands out of desire for relatively proximity to telcos, and London’s banking/finance industry.
children.textZhHtml:
伦敦在斯劳（希思罗附近）和 Docklands（伦敦城市机场，但也有许多 LHR 飞机中转）有很多数据中心。

AWS/Azure/GCP/etc Colo 位于 Equinix/Telehouse 数据中心，特别是那些 Docklands 位置是根据 LINX（主要的伦敦对等互连/交换）的位置来选择的，LINX 被放置在 Docklands 之外希望相对靠近电信公司和伦敦的银行/金融业。

children.author: throwaway2037
children.textRawHtml: Were those obviously hardened to withstand the impact of an jet aeroplane?  I doubt it.
children.textZhHtml: 那些明显经过加固可以承受喷气式飞机的冲击吗？  我对此表示怀疑。

children.author: yardstick
children.textRawHtml:
Semi-related, there are some very cool converted datacentres in the UK.

The Bunker operates an underground datacentre out of a former military installation. Radar base if memory serves me. That’s definitely hardened from airplane attacks and I believe is used by some hyperscalers.

https://thebunker.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/The-Bunker-...
children.textZhHtml:
半相关的是，英国有一些非常酷的改建数据中心。

The Bunker 在前军事设施中运营着一个地下数据中心。如果我没记错的话，雷达基地。这绝对是通过飞机攻击而得到强化的，我相信一些超大规模企业正在使用它。

https://thebunker.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/The-Bunker-...

children.author: yardstick
children.textRawHtml: No idea, just answering the “Why not pick a location not within a "major airport flight path"? It seems much cheaper.” question.
children.textZhHtml: 不知道，只是回答“为什么不选择不在“主要机场航线”内的位置？看起来便宜得多。”问题。<!--文章-->

children.author: bombcar
children.textRawHtml: At least one colo facility I’ve been was an ex-defense facility. And it had reasons to be where it was, and to be hardened.
children.textZhHtml: 我去过的至少一处托管设施是前国防设施。它有理由存在并得到强化。

children.author: Someone
children.textRawHtml:
> It probably wouldn't help much against ballistic missiles, but it might make it more resilient against drone attacks.

I think the two kinds of attacks are so different that they require different defenses.

Drones need not fly in straight lines. Data centers need ventilation, providing a path for drones. Putting grids in a ventilation shaft will stop the first drone, but a coordinated attack will use one drone to blow up defenses and a second/third/etc one to reach the target
children.textZhHtml:
> 它可能对对抗弹道导弹没有多大帮助，但它可能会使其对无人机攻击更有弹性。

我认为这两种攻击非常不同，因此需要不同的防御。

无人机不需要直线飞行。数据中心需要通风，为无人机提供通道。将网格放入通风井将阻止第一架无人机，但协调攻击将使用一架无人机炸毁防御，然后使用第二架/第三架/等等无人机到达目标

children.author: nazgulnarsil
children.textRawHtml: And presumably eventually those exhaust ports would be obfuscated, necessitating the stealing of plans to identify such vulnerabilities.
children.textZhHtml: 大概最终这些排气口会被混淆，从而需要窃取识别此类漏洞的计划。

children.author: Someone
children.textRawHtml: Heat is relatively hard to hide. The best solution likely spreads it out over a large area, creating a building with myriads of tiny holes.
children.textZhHtml: 热量相对难以隐藏。最好的解决方案可能是将其分散到一个大的区域，创建一个带有无数小孔的建筑物。

children.author: londons_explore
children.textRawHtml:
It is probably far cheaper to simply have global redundancy for the data and compute than to put the datacenter in a bunker.

Tell everyone that you have global redundancy and they won't even bother to damage it because it won't help their cause.
children.textZhHtml:
简单地为数据和计算提供全局冗余可能比将数据中心放入地堡要便宜得多。

告诉每个人您拥有全局冗余，他们甚至不会费心去破坏它，因为这对他们的事业没有帮助。

children.author: donalhunt
children.textRawHtml: Not all businesses want to pay the premium for that level of redundancy. Businesses with lower margins want resilient service at a lower price point. With AI and contributed shift to cloud, the demand for lowering TCO for a greater share of the larger pie becomes greater.
children.textZhHtml: 并非所有企业都愿意为这种程度的冗余支付额外费用。利润率较低的企业希望以较低的价格获得弹性服务。随着人工智能和向云计算的转变，降低总体拥有成本以获取更大份额的需求变得更大。

children.author: londons_explore
children.textRawHtml: If they don't want to spend the $ for redundancy, they definitely don't want to spend the $$$ for a war-proof datacenter.
children.textZhHtml: 如果他们不想花美元用于冗余，他们绝对不想花美元购买防战数据中心。

children.author: vasco
children.textRawHtml: It's sad but also interesting that in someone's disaster recovery plan now they need to add a line item about analyzing which datacenters are behind air defenses.
children.textZhHtml: 令人悲伤但也很有趣的是，在某人的灾难恢复计划中，现在他们需要添加一个有关分析哪些数据中心位于防空系统后面的行项目。
